seeker: Hey. Not great, to be honest. Just got some feedback on my thesis that's really got me down.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about what they said?
seeker: Yeah, sure. My advisor thought it lacked depth and wasn't very clear in parts. It feels like so much work just went down the drain.
supporter: That sounds really frustrating. You've put so much effort into this. It makes sense that you'd feel discouraged.
seeker: Yeah, and it's just on top of everything else. Things with Jenny aren't great either. We argued about my career priorities last week.
supporter: It seems like there's a lot going on for you right now. The argument with Jenny must be weighing heavily on your mind too.
seeker: It is. I'm just feeling like I'm not making anyone happy, including myself.
supporter: It makes sense you'd feel that way. Sometimes when things stack up, it feels overwhelming. What do you think might help right now?
seeker: Honestly, I don't even know. Maybe just talking it through with someone helps a bit, like this conversation.
supporter: That's good to hear. I'm here to listen. You're not alone in this, even if it feels like it sometimes.
seeker: Thanks. I guess with everything happening, I just forgot how to take care of myself for a bit.
supporter: It's understandable. Self-care is often the first thing we overlook when life's pressures pile up. Is there anything small you can do for yourself today?
seeker: Maybe I'll take a walk. It usually clears my head, even if just a bit.
supporter: That sounds like a great idea. Fresh air and a change of scenery can work wonders.
seeker: Yeah, I should do that more. I generally get lost in my work these days.
supporter: It can be easy to get caught up, especially when there's pressure to perform. Do you feel like you're getting enough support from those around you?

seeker: Maybe. I'll have to see. I just wish things would settle down.
supporter: It's understandable to feel that way. It's clear you're dealing with a lot right now. Having someone to talk to each step of the way can make it just a bit easier.
seeker: Yeah. I'm glad I reached out today. It helps to get some perspective.
supporter: Anytime, Andrew. You're doing your best, and that's all anyone can ask right now.
seeker: Thanks for listening. I needed it.

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hey Andrew, how have you been feeling lately?
seeker: Hey, honestly, I've been a bit overwhelmed. I'm considering changing my research focus, and it's been weighing on me.
supporter: I can imagine that must be a tough decision. What’s making you think about changing your focus?
seeker: I haven't made much progress lately, and I'm just not interested in my current topic anymore. Plus, the feedback from my advisor was disheartening.
supporter: That sounds really frustrating. Feedback like that can really bring you down, especially when you're already feeling uncertain. How did you feel after hearing it?
seeker: I felt a bit lost, to be honest. Like I’m just not cut out for this. It's hard because it makes me question my decisions.
supporter: It's completely normal to question yourself when you're going through such challenges. Remember, you’ve made it this far for a reason. What do you think would rekindle your interest in research?
seeker: I've been considering exploring alternative energy sources, like renewables. It's something that aligns with my values and seems rewarding.
supporter: That sounds exciting and definitely impactful! How do you feel when you think about making that shift?
seeker: It feels kind of refreshing, like it might give me the motivation I’ve been lacking. But I'm still worried about the implications, like how much time it would take to adjust.
supporter: Change can be daunting, but if it brings you closer to something you’re passionate about, it might be worth the effort. Have you talked to your advisor or any peers about this possibility?
seeker: Not yet. I wanted to be sure about my own feelings before bringing it up, but I guess I need to have that conversation soon.
supporter: That makes sense. Having clarity on your end first is important. How about Jenny? Have you shared your thoughts with her?
seeker: Not in depth. Things have been a bit tense between us since we had that conversation about our future plans.
supporter: It's important to be open with her, especially since this is a significant part of your life. It could even help ease some of the tension.
seeker: You're right. It's just tricky because I worry about adding more stress to our relationship.
supporter: It’s understandable to worry about that. But open communication can sometimes help in easing worries by building more understanding. Maybe when you feel ready, have a gentle conversation with her?
seeker: That’s a good point. I'll try to approach it with more openness. It might even help both of us.
supporter: I'm really glad to hear that. Remember, you’re not alone in this. I’m here whenever you need to talk.
seeker: Thank you. That really means a lot. It’s nice knowing I have someone to turn to.
supporter: Always. Take it one step at a time, and don't hesitate to reach out again. You’ve got this.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-01-01","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hi Andrew! I hope you're doing okay. What's been on your mind lately?
seeker: Hey, thanks for checking in. Honestly, I've been feeling really anxious lately about my future career. It's been weighing on me a lot.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Career worries can be incredibly stressful. Do you mind sharing a bit more about what's been causing this anxiety?
seeker: Yeah, it's like I was already feeling a bit uncertain after the feedback I got on my thesis a while ago, and now I'm considering changing my research focus because I feel stuck and uninterested.
supporter: I remember you mentioning the feedback you received being quite discouraging. It makes sense that you're feeling this way. What about changing your research focus is making you anxious?
seeker: It's the uncertainty, I guess. I'm worried about making the wrong choice and derailing my entire career path. And with everything else going on with Jenny, it's just a lot to handle.
supporter: It sounds like you're carrying a heavy burden. Balancing relationship issues with career decisions must be extremely overwhelming. Have you had a chance to talk with Jenny about how you're feeling?
seeker: We tried talking about it after New Year's, but it didn't go too well. We're still on different pages regarding our career and family plans, and that added pressure isn't helping my anxiety.
supporter: I'm really sorry things are tough between you and Jenny. Have you thought more about the idea of couples counseling to help with communication?
seeker: Yeah, I have. I think it might be a good idea, but I'm not sure how to bring it up again without causing another argument.
supporter: It's definitely a delicate situation. Maybe framing it as a way for both of you to understand each other better rather than as a problem might help?
seeker: That makes sense. I could give it a try. I just wish I didn't feel so isolated through all of this. Even when I try to socialize, like when I game online, it’s not the same.
supporter: Feeling isolated can really compound stress and anxiety. It's great that you're trying to connect, even if it's online. Have you thought about reaching out to your friends again, or maybe even joining a group with similar interests?
seeker: I haven't thought of that, but it might help. I did feel a bit distant after I confronted them about excluding me, so I'm not sure how receptive they'd be.
supporter: That must have been tough to deal with, especially getting mixed reactions from them. Perhaps finding a new group could open up some positive experiences and connections?
seeker: Yeah, exploring new groups sounds like it could be a good move. I should try to put myself out there more, even if it feels intimidating.
supporter: It's totally understandable to feel intimidated, but taking small steps might make it less daunting. Remember, it's okay to feel anxious, and you're taking positive steps by reaching out and considering your options.
seeker: Thanks for the encouragement. I do feel a bit better knowing I'm at least trying to figure things out. Talking about it helps.
supporter: I'm really glad to hear that. Remember, you're not alone in this, and it's great that you're taking the time to consider what will truly make you happy. I'm here anytime you need to talk.
seeker: I appreciate it a lot. I'll keep you updated on how things go with Jenny and my research focus.
supporter: Please do! I'm sure things will start looking up. Take care of yourself, Andrew.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2025-01-05","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: How can I help you today?
seeker: I'm disgusted with my professors that they don't see me as a human with real emotions and feelings.
supporter: I understand that you are feeling like your professors don't see you as a person with feelings. What happened to make you feel this way?
seeker: I have testing all the time and study non-stop, but the professors don't seem to encourage or support me.  They just see me as a number I feel.
supporter: That's hard to feel like they are treating you like a number when you are working so hard.  Have you talked to them about it?
seeker: It's hard to trust them when I'm seen as 1 of 100 people.  If I am struggling they don't flinch or ask me how they can assist.  I just am expected to 
seeker: tough it out.
supporter: I had a similar experience in my college days. It was very difficult to have so much pressure to succeed and feel so alone.  You can do though because you are working hard and want to succeed.
seeker: Thanks for the encouragement.  Where do I start to help myself feel better?
supporter: I see you are anxious about this when talking to you, but have you thought about getting some support from other students in your position?
seeker: That sounds like a good idea.  Maybe they are feeling this way too.
supporter: Also sometimes just stepping back and taking some deep breaths can help to alleviate some anxieties. Have you tried that ever?
seeker: I will have to give that a try.  I've done that in the past and had forgotten just how much that helped me before.  
supporter: That is reassuring that it worked before for you and  can work again.
seeker: I'm so worried about failing because I just don't feel the support from my professors to care either way for my successes.  It's so different from high school and home when my parents encouraged me and supported me full-heartedly.  
supporter: College can be quite a change from the protective atmosphere of home.  Have you tried any support groups or religious groups for encouragement?
seeker: I am religious so perhaps I could seek a group out and they could help with encouraging me.  
supporter: I was a  part of a religious group in college and they were very supportive even praying for me on exam days.  I felt they helped me with my success by planting seeds of positive feedback to me.
seeker: I used to be part of one during high school years, and that sounds like it would help.
supporter: Are you starting to feel better about the situation?
seeker: Yes, I do thinking about other people filling in the gaps and supporting me when others won't or can't. Thanks for chatting.  This was helpful.
supporter: You are welcome.  I wish you well.

memory.content:
{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hello there! How can I encourage you today?
seeker: Hi, I have been going through a lot of stress with school and am also sad and lonely as of late and not sure how to make myself feel better
supporter: So you have had a lot of stress with school lately and are struggling to keep yourself cheerful?
supporter: Is there something in particular at school that is stressing you out? Exams? Relationships?
seeker: Yes! Its very hard to keep positive with all the work I have and I feel I am not doing well.
seeker: Yes, I have a lot of exams right now and that on top of not hanging out with friends a lot lately has made life tough.
supporter: I can understand being stressed if you think you are not doing well in school and have a lot of work. How are your grades now?
seeker: I still have decent grades but I feel like I am not prepared for big exams currently and they are worth a lot
supporter: Yes, that can be tough. When I had a lot of tests coming up and a lot to study for, I wrote down goals to study -- like I broke down the classes and made certain goals to study a bit in each class. And then if I did that, I could go out with friends or some reward like that. 
supporter: For example, if you have 7 classes, you can make a chart for when you will study for each of those classes and then check them off as you accomplish it, maybe not all in one day, maybe break it up in reasonable bits. Then study according to your goal, if that makes sense.
supporter: I remember after each class, I would take 15 minutes to review all my notes from class, that seems short, but really, it adds up and helped so much.
seeker: Yes, I think you have excellent advice about organization. I feel like I lose track of what I have and when to do it. I also bounce between classes, feeling stressed because there is so much. Do you think doing one class at a time is best?
seeker: I also tend to save stuff sometimes so I have a lot of work build up with tests on the same days. I am not sure how to stop procrastinating.
supporter: Yes, stick to one subject at a time. For example, if you think 1/2 hour is good enough to study, then stick to that. When done, your done until the next time it is on your schedule.
seeker: Ok. Thank you so much for the ideas. It seems like you have had similar experiences with stress from school.
supporter: Procrastination never makes us feel good. If I keep putting something off, I then feel guilty. If I make a goal, and I reach it, I can put a reward. For example, if you study 3 subjects 1/2 hour each, you can go out for yogurt with a friend. So you reward yourself for sticking to that goal.
supporter: Yes, I did. lol I'm really old now. This technique I use in all my life. Even house chores, I break it down into a schedule, put it in writing, then check off what I do. Then I feel good about my accomplishments.
seeker: Yes, that was my other question to you. It sounds great to just do a little time for each class but I often get overwhelmed and need a break
seeker: I have never used check lists or planners. I think it is part of how I get overwhelmed maybe.
supporter: Definitely you need a break, so schedule them as rewards. You can even do 15 minutes in say 4 subjects, then take a walk, take a cup of tea, or call a friend, then back to the books. 
supporter: Keep it as SIMPLE as possible, don't get bogged down. I used to think planning was TERRIBLE< but actually, it sets one FREE. You feel so much better and accomplished when you see how much you have done. It really is amazing. 
supporter: HOw man classes do you have?
supporter: many *
seeker: I have 6 classes
supporter: That's a lot but it is totally doable. Here is a good example, If you plant seeds in a garden today, you have to weed it a bit tomorrow, the next day, the next day, you have to wait for rain, then weed some more, the harvest comes and YAY! You are happy. But if you lie on your bed, never planting, never weeding, you procrastinate, you get nothing.
supporter: If you write your classes down and then write a reasonable time to study each one. Maybe 3 today, 3 tomorrow, then add rewards if you do that, maybe make a list of rewards, so you can pick and choose, then you check off when you do the subject.  Like a chore chart. 
seeker: Yes haha. That is a good comparison. You have been super helpful. I will for sure try to use your advice. Thank you!
seeker: Have a great day and thanks again
supporter: You are quite welcome! God bless have a great day!","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-06-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}
